text:
sasha: Kicking off a small thread to lock down the Private Deploy roadmap slice for upgrades + customer-managed networking. Main goals: define patch vs minor/major flows, installer UX choices, and the relay/BGP fallback story.

matt: Good call. Sales wants near-zero disruption for patch releases; legal wants clarity on egress-handling for any relay solution.

julio: From the field: two enterprise customers require preserved source IPs after upgrade and a sample BGP config. They also run behind NAT appliances with asymmetric routing.

kai: Draft acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Patch updates perform hotpatch with canary and <1% error rate; 2) Minor/major upgrades support rollback to previous operator within 5min; 3) Installer exposes "egress_mode" (direct_peer | relay) and documents tradeoffs; 4) KMS rotation demo + audit log.

netops: For relay we need a template and security contract. Relay config minimal payload: `relay_host`, `bgp_asn`, `peer_ip`, `allowed_prefixes`, `tls_cert_id`. Relay must be auditable and preserve advertised egress IPs in TCP/UDP flows.

matt: On technical approach: two upgrade primitives: hotpatch (binary delta apply retaining in-memory KV) vs operator-bundle restart (blue/green). Hotpatch lowers customer-visible downtime but requires stronger compatibility checks (kv checksum, ABI invariants).

sasha: @matt can you run a risk matrix? Hotpatch cons: ABI drift, state model mismatch, harder crash recovery. Pros: much lower SLO impact for embeddings/chat.

matt: Will do. Prototype plan: agent that receives a signed patch, runs preflight version-check, applies delta, runs `kv-corr` verification, then opens traffic if OK. CLI for testbed:

```
redwood-operator upgrade --strategy hotpatch --canary 0.05 --verify-scripts ./checks/kv-check.sh
```

This stages on 5% and runs kv integrity checks.

julio: Add compatibility test matrix: operator X -> SDK Y behaviors (esp embeddings and streaming). We saw subtle framing changes earlier.

netops: For customers who decline peering, relay-proxy must be first-class: HA pair, clear throughput billing, and an SLA for IP-preservation. Also legal needs a short terms blurb.

kai: Launch gates: (A) e2e acceptance across aws + gcp + onprem runner; (B) 3-customer beta for 6 weeks; (C) runbooks & rollback playbooks + incident drill; (D) pricing buckets and SLA table.

matt: deploy-bot: staging report?

deploy-bot: Staging: operator-v1.4.3-hotpatch passed smoke on gcp-europe-west1 at 2024-08-05T09:40:12Z. kv-checksum: ok, canary-requests: 1500, errors: 2 (timed-out).

matt: Great. Please log `kv-checksum` output to CI artifacts for future triage.

julio: Action items: Sasha -> scope doc with acceptance + opt-in defaults; Matt -> hotpatch prototype + integration tests by next Wed; Netops -> BGP + relay template and compliance note by Tue.

sasha: Default opt-in posture: enable hotpatch by default for semver.patch, but installer shows explicit consent toggle and records decision in audit log. Add `force_restart=true` flag for customers who want deterministic restarts.

kai: Costing rule: Relay usage >50% of egress traffic = billable add-on (instance-hours + egress). Need product pricing stub.

matt: One open question: do we require customers to acknowledge potential limitations (e.g., kernel-level incompat) before hotpatch? My vote: show a short EULA-like checkbox in installer and log the acceptance.

sasha: Agreed; surface the risk and record acceptance. Also add an installer UI row: Upgrade Safety Level (Hotpatch | Bundled Restart) with a short help tooltip.

julio: CS note: prepare beta comms telling customers: "expected downtime: near-zero for patch updates, brief window for minors/majors".

netops: Legal/security requested a template line for IP-handling: "Relay will not store payload data; only connection metadata retained for troubleshooting". I'll seek signoff.

kai: Timeline check: prototype + staging tests = 3 weeks; beta kickoff Q3 week 4; GA targeted end of Q3 if beta is clean. Blockers?

matt: Prototype fragility is the biggest risk. Fallback: use blue/green for patch channel until hotpatch stabilizes.

sasha: I'll assemble a one-pager decision record + acceptance matrix and circulate. Will include the patch/compat matrix mapping operator versions to supported SDKs.

deploy-bot: Reminder: Release sync in #eng-releases tomorrow 10:00.

sasha: Thanks everyone. I'll post the one-pager and link it in this thread. :thumbsup:

matt: Adding `kv-checksum` CI checks and cross-version integration tests.

julio: Netops, ping me once the BGP sample is ready so CS can review.

Thread summary (sasha): hotpatch-by-default for patch releases; bundle/blue-green for minor/major; relay-proxy as fallback for non-peering customers; BGP + IP-preservation templates required; acceptance gates and action items assigned.
